canonical_question: Does the propagation of cracks from the surface to the RHEA substrate interface suggest a critical weakness in the double-layer structure?

question_variants.question: Does the propagation of cracks from the surface to the RHEA substrate interface suggest a critical weakness in the double-layer structure?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text confirms crack propagation to the interface but does not explicitly conclude whether this indicates a critical weakness or the failure mode of the structure.

answers.answer: The text reports that cracks propagated to the interface, but does not interpret this as a critical weakness or provide an assessment of the double-layer structure's inherent failure susceptibility.
answers.measurement_outcome: cracks propagated from surface to interface between silicide coating and RHEA substrate
answers.boundary_limitation: Interpretation of crack significance not provided.
evidence_spans: In this paper, the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating was prepared on MoNbTaTiW RHEA by a fused slurry method.
The microstructural evolution and compositions of the silicide coating under high-temperature oxidation environment were studied.
The results show that the silicide coating could effectively prevent the oxidation of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA.

source_evidence_spans: It also can be seen that some cracks propagated from the surface to the inner layer of the silicide coating and even to the interface between the silicide coating and the RHEA substrate.
